rule: Every view the user has flagged is rendered from its cameras for the candidate and the live release, next to the photograph where a panorama exists, before any publish (check_flagged_views.py writes <candidate>/flagged-views/; publish_full_candidate_v24.py refuses a candidate without it). The sheets are looked at at native resolution. A defect listed here is reported as fixed only when its sheet shows it gone from these cameras; a new defect seen on a sheet is added here. Coordinates are scene metres (x east, y north, z up; ground here is about 2.3 m). This file is review data for checking releases; the generator never reads it. Each flagged camera with a panorama also compares the flagged building's wall colour with the photograph (check_flagged_views.py, dE with lightness at half weight > 18 blocks publishing, --known-mismatch only for a registered open defect the release does not touch and no worse than live).

cameras.name: street-corner-southwest
cameras.note: reported 2026-09-28 (Street mode): the tall building's alley frontage in white render with lilac and salmon panels and a thin wall at the corner; photographs show a set-back dark glass and metal block with a glazed rooftop pavilion

views.expected: One outline holds two buildings. On the corner, a one-storey brick building: stepped parapet on the main-street front, a pitched roof behind it (LiDAR eaves about 6.8 m, ridge about 9.9 m, ridge running front to back), an arched door and a large arched opening. Set back behind it and running along the alley, a taller, newer building of dark glass and dark metal with a glazed rooftop pavilion and roof planting. No tall wall stands at the alley corner. No panorama sees the tall building's alley facade.

defects.text: A thin wall of the tall part stands at the alley corner and rises about 15 m past the low building.
defects.cause: building_parts.split hands the leftover edge strip (0.3-0.7 m wide) to the largest part.

defects.text: Stepped volumes behind the low building.
defects.cause: The part boundary follows the 2 m LiDAR grid, which runs at 45 degrees to this outline.

defects.text: The tall building's alley facade changes material and windows between releases (white in v0.14-v0.15, v0.22 and v0.28; brick in between).
defects.cause: No photograph; it is decided by fallback rules (a material vote over the readings of both parts, then the apartment prior) that changed in v0.16, v0.22, v0.23, v0.25 and v0.28.

defects.text: The alley-corner walls carry readings of a half-occluded photograph (pink brick, a dark door that is the neighbour's base).
defects.cause: The occlusion test is a 2D footprint check with no margin; the sight lines pass 0.03-3.8 m from the building across the alley and the camera pose is good to about 2.5 m.

defects.text: The low building's pitched roof is drawn flat.
defects.cause: Tilted roof planes need 150 m2 each; each slope here is about 100 m2.

defects.text: The taller building shows pale render or brick; the photographs show dark glass and dark metal.
defects.cause: Its photographed part (seen above the low building from the main street) is never read; the main-street reading covers only the low building's frontage, and it is the one that votes for the tall building's material.

views.expected: From the street: a tall arcade storey with large arched glazed openings and a roof terrace (cast stone on the south side), and behind and above it the upper deck's structure as open dark-green steel framing with brick stair towers at corners, light rigs on top. Floors step back in level tiers; nothing is a draped surface.

defects.text: The grandstand back is a draped brick surface with vertical drips over the arcade.
defects.cause: The whole stands structure was one triangulated LiDAR surface; steep parts facing away from the field were typed brick and the outline wall rose to the surface's noisy edge.

defects.text: The south arcade storey is brick in the model; the photographs show cast stone with large arched glazed openings and a roof terrace railing. Fixed: stone read from the panoramas in its measured colour, glazed segmental arches, terrace railing.
defects.cause: The outline wall takes one material all round; only one stretch of the outline has a reading.

defects.text: Inside the south edge a few low blocks with rounded outlines stand at different floor levels (pits and raised pieces of the terrace level).
defects.cause: LiDAR clutter on the terrace larger than the 150 m2 clutter rule, levelled to separate floors.

defects.text: A set-back brick wall stood above the arcade terrace where the photographs show the steel superstructure.
defects.cause: Two short floor walls stacked there were each under the 5 m steel rule; the rule now uses the height above the street.

cameras.name: user-report-across-street
cameras.note: reported 2026-09-29 (street level, looking up at the south corner): scalloped blank brick wall, stacked projecting boxes with white cornices, corner bays, a low brick wing with a garage opening; 'deviates extremely heavily from its real-life counterpart'

views.expected: A six-storey office block clad in small red-brown ceramic tile, standing on a raised planted podium. Every storey is a continuous ribbon of dark glazing between solid tile spandrel bands; the bands wrap round rounded corners (LiDAR shows about 2-3 m radius at the south and east corners). The top storey is set back about 4 m behind a ledge at about 22 m (LiDAR 26.3 m top, a plant room to about 31 m), and toward the north-west the block steps down in storey-high terraces (LiDAR about 13.8, 10.7 and 7 m). The podium is a blank tile planter wall about 3-4 m high with a white dentil course and a red cap, shrubs and trees on top, and a curved glass entrance canopy at the east corner. A fenced vacant lot lies to the south-west.

defects.text: The block's set-back faces are scalloped zig-zag brick walls.
defects.cause: Tier outlines are polygonised from a north-up 1.5 m roof raster; on a footprint at 45 degrees they keep the cell staircase (about 300 vertices per tier).

defects.text: One vertical block is drawn as three stacked boxes (4-10.8, 10.8-19, 19-22.3 m) with a cornice and white ledge at each join.
defects.cause: Consecutive superlevel tiers of one vertical wall are merged only when their independently simplified outlines differ by under one cell; drifting staircases never do. Each tier then draws its own wall, base band and cornice.

defects.text: The set-back top storey is missing; the model stops at about 22-23 m.
defects.cause: The three duplicate slices used the tier budget (lidarRole tierMaxCount 3), which keeps the lowest tiers and drops the top ones.

defects.text: Punched windows, projecting boxes and corner bays where the photographs show continuous ribbon windows between tile spandrel bands.
defects.cause: The set-back faces are never read from the photographs (tier walls, staircase facets); walls take the commercial prior's window grid with sills, jambs and cornices.

defects.text: The podium walls carry dark garage-like openings and shopfront glazing; the photographs show a blank planter wall.
defects.cause: The hand reading of the planter wall carries the 21.4 m frame height, so the low-blank-wall continuity rule (reading height 6 m or less) never applies to the podium's other walls.

defects.text: Corners are square; the building's corners are rounded.
defects.cause: Outlines keep polygon corners; nothing measures a corner radius.

defects.text: Brick texture where the building is clad in small square tiles.
defects.cause: The reader classes the red-brown colour as brick; no tile family is read.
